children: Southern California Edison today announced additional opportunities for community members directly impacted by the Eaton Fire to learn more about the
and get help submitting claims before the Nov. 30 deadline. The series includes SCE-hosted virtual and in-person community meetings as well as participation in events throughout the community.

“As the Nov. 30 deadline approaches, we encourage community members to understand all of the options available to them,” said Pedro J. Pizarro, president and CEO of Edison International, SCE’s parent company. “These events provide a convenient way to ask questions, get support and determine the next steps that are right for their situation.”
Just over two months remain to
. Eligible community members who do not submit a claim by Nov. 30, 2026, will not have the opportunity to learn what compensation may be available to them through the program.
Submitting a claim, receiving an offer and evaluating that offer do not waive a claimant’s rights.
On average, SCE delivers offers 36 days after receiving a substantially complete claim.
Community members who believe a Fast Pay offer does not adequately reflect their losses may request a Detailed Review. To preserve that option, they must submit a claim by Nov. 30, 2026.
To submit a claim and access detailed guidance in English and Spanish, visit the

children: . One-on-one assistance is available in multiple languages by phone or in person, from start to finish. Call 888-912-8528 to get started.
Nearly 4,900 claims submitted, consisting of more than 14,900 individuals, trusts and legal entities, with 40% submitted by attorneys or authorized representatives.
Nearly 2,800 offers extended to over 6,900 claimants, totaling more than $970 million.
More than 3,700 claimants paid, totaling over $525 million, with many more in process.
Register for a Virtual or In-Person Session
SCE will host the following virtual and in-person sessions where community members can learn about the program, ask questions and receive help starting a claim:
Tuesday, Oct. 13, 6 p.m. (rebuild-focused community meeting in Irwindale)
